# Diffusion-guided editing
## Overview
Diffusion-guided editing modifies pre-trained NeRFs by leveraging 2D text-to-image diffusion models as external priors to guide 3D appearance and geometry changes [S1]. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods by either iteratively updating the training dataset with diffusion-edited views [14365-repaint-nerf.md] or directly backpropagating photometric losses from edited renders to update NeRF parameters [15089-instruct-nerf2nerf-optimization.md], rather than relying solely on semantic masks or geometric constraints [S1]. This family builds on [NeRF Editing and Inpainting Procedures](12494-nerf-editing-and-inpainting-procedures.md) [G].
## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [RePaint-NeRF](14365-repaint-nerf.md)
Iteratively alternates between editing input images with a diffusion model and retraining the NeRF on the updated dataset to propagate 2D edits into 3D space while preserving view consistency [14365-repaint-nerf.md]. Choose when scene integrity and multi-view consistency are prioritized over direct gradient guidance.

### [Instruct-NeRF2NeRF Optimization](15089-instruct-nerf2nerf-optimization.md)
Directly backpropagates photometric loss between rendered views and InstructPix2Pix-edited views to update NeRF parameters without iterative dataset replacement [15089-instruct-nerf2nerf-optimization.md]. Choose for instruction-based editing where classifier-free guidance weights control edit strength, accepting subjective termination due to stochastic diffusion outputs.

### MALD-NeRF
Employs a per-scene customization latent diffusion model to generate inpainted images and iteratively updates the training set [S1]. It incorporates a masked patch-based adversarial training strategy with adversarial loss and discriminator feature matching losses to refine results, using a pixel-level regression loss for reconstruction [S1].

## Background
Diffusion-guided editing emerged to address inconsistencies when applying 2D edits to 3D scenes independently [S1]. Recent advancements increasingly explore inpainting techniques on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) due to its rendering efficiency and high-quality reconstruction, while methods like MALD-NeRF refine results through adversarial training and iterative dataset updates [S1].
## Sources
